label: City
_model: Settlement kernel at its largest. Nobody here knows anybody, so the city knows instead — by ward, by roll, by works, by freedom granted and withheld. Its cruelties are all administrative, which is why none of them can be argued with.

appetites.want: never to be equalled by anywhere else
appetites.purpose: it would be the greatest thing ever built

appeasement.move: praise something the city built, specifically, and out loud
appeasement.why: it was admired for what it made

appetites.want: that nobody within its walls should be unaccounted for
appetites.purpose: every soul would be on a roll somewhere

appeasement.move: give your name and your parish, in full, to be written down

appetites.want: that everything should be in its proper ward
appetites.purpose: nothing would ever be where it should not be

appeasement.move: put one thing back exactly where the city says it belongs
appeasement.why: it is where it should be

appetites.want: that no power outside its walls should reach inside them
appetites.purpose: nothing here would ever answer to anybody else

appeasement.move: claim the freedom of the city aloud, and then act as though you had it

accommodations.text: conscripted {conscript} onto the works and never signed their release
moved {conscript} from ward to ward until no ward would own them
enrolled {conscript} so thoroughly that they could not exist anywhere else
built over the street {conscript} lived in, with {conscript} still in it
made {conscript} free of the city, which cost them their freedom everywhere else
struck {conscript} off every roll, so that the city could say they had never come

keystone.label: the keystone cut for the arch that was never closed
keystone.function: the only piece of the works that would have finished it

roll.label: the roll with every name on it, including the struck-off
roll.function: the only record here that was never corrected

chain.label: the chain of office, still warm
chain.function: the only thing here that everything obeyed without asking why

gate.label: the key of the postern that is not on any plan
gate.function: the only way in or out the city never controlled

factions.name: the City
factions.essence: still administering, still expecting everyone to be from somewhere

factions.name: the incomers
factions.essence: came in for the work and were never enrolled

factions.name: the Wardmote
factions.essence: will not let anything stand in the wrong ward

factions.name: what lives under the streets
factions.essence: was built over and did not move out

triggerGlossary.announced: came in at a gate and gave a name to the man on it
triggerGlossary.seenTwice: noticed in two different wards on the same day
triggerGlossary.loud: a raised voice in a street with windows above it
triggerGlossary.lingering: stood in one ward long enough for the Wardmote to want you accounted for
triggerGlossary.disturbed: opened a grating, moved a boundary mark, or went into the works

foes.name: Bandit
foes.note: know every alley; will vanish rather than die

skirmish.avoid: they are working the ward, not hunting you — walk into another ward and they stop

fight.line: 4 Bandits and a Hobgoblin Soldier as ward constable

foes.name: Hobgoblin Soldier
foes.note: demands to know your ward before it strikes

fight.avoid: name a ward convincingly and the constable calls them off

battle.line: 1 Necromancer of the Chamber and 4 Skeletons in livery

foes.name: Necromancer
foes.note: raises one Skeleton per round off the charnel ground

battle.harmedBy: anything — the Necromancer is alive and bleeds
battle.avoid: it is enrolling the dead; give it a name for the roll and it must stop to write

nightmare.line: 1 Wraith of the Lord Mayor, 1 Necromancer and 5 Skeletons

foes.name: Wraith
foes.note: INCORPOREAL — chill touch ignores armour, drains 1 max Grit

nightmare.harmedBy: blessed, silvered or magical weapons for the Wraith ONLY; anything for the rest
nightmare.avoid: do not run this without an appeasement route open

works.dangerLine: the city is still building, and it does not release anyone it has taken on

institution: scaffolding grown into the buildings it was raised against
a mason's lodge with the drawings pinned up and current
cranes on every roofline, all of them loaded
ritual: a course of stone laid each day whether or not there is anyone to lay it
the bell for the shift rung at the same hour
a drawing checked against the work and initialled
demand: an arch standing open with the keystone cut and set aside
a course of stone laid and the next course marked out
a hod filled and left at the foot of a ladder
wound: a crane loaded and the rope cut
a lodge with the drawings still pinned and the tools gone
an arch that came down and was built again over what fell
anchor: the keystone cut for the arch that was never closed
the master drawing, complete and to scale
a mason's mark on every good stone in the city

features: a hod filled at the foot of a ladder
a keystone set aside beside its arch
a course marked out in chalk
a crane loaded with the rope cut
drawings pinned and current
a mason's mark cut fresh

decisions.cue: an arch standing open with the keystone cut and set aside
decisions.cost: setting it closes the arch, and closes something else

resolve.success: you set the keystone and the works stop for the first time — the city exhales, and a way opens
resolve.failure: it slips, and the arch takes it out on whatever is beneath: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave the arch open; the works go on and the shift bell keeps ringing

decisions.cue: a hod filled and left at the foot of a ladder
decisions.cost: picking it up puts you on the shift

resolve.success: you carry one hod up and the works accept you — you can walk the scaffold anywhere
resolve.failure: you carry it and cannot put it down until the shift bell rings: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave the hod; the scaffold will not take your weight

decisions.cue: a master drawing pinned up and initialled to today's date
decisions.cost: somebody is still checking the work

resolve.success: you find who is initialling and they will show you what the works were really for
resolve.failure: you alter the drawing and the works build it exactly as altered
resolve.orElse: leave it; the works continue to a plan you do not know

decisions.cue: a crane loaded and the rope cut, the load still up there
decisions.cost: the load can be brought down or left

resolve.success: you bring it down safely and the lodge is grateful, and opens
resolve.failure: you cut it loose and it comes down on the street: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it hanging; it hangs over every route through this quarter

decisions.cue: a course of stone laid today, in a city with nobody in it
decisions.cost: the next course is marked out in chalk

resolve.success: you lay the next course correctly and the works count you as one of their own
resolve.failure: you lay it wrong and the whole run has to come down, with you on it
resolve.orElse: leave the chalk; you are trespass on the works, not labour

decisions.cue: a mason's mark cut fresh into a stone laid centuries ago
decisions.cost: the mark says who is still working

resolve.success: you match the mark and can find the mason, who wants releasing and will trade for it
resolve.failure: you cut your own mark beside it and are on the works' books: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave the stone; the mason keeps working and nobody finds them

situations.doing: cutting a stone that is already finished
situations.onArrival: it holds the chisel out to you rather than speak
situations.because: the stone was never signed off and the shift never ended
situations.offer: take a single stroke for it and it will cut you through any wall here

situations.doing: carrying a hod up a ladder into empty air
situations.onArrival: the top of the ladder reaches nothing at all
situations.because: the course must go up and the scaffold came down
situations.offer: tell them the course is finished and they will carry you up instead

situations.doing: standing under an open arch with a keystone at its feet
situations.onArrival: it looks up at the gap and then at you
situations.because: the arch cannot be closed by anyone still on the books
situations.offer: close the arch and it will release anything the works hold

situations.doing: chalking a course onto a wall that already has one
situations.onArrival: they ask whether the drawing has been revised
situations.because: they were sent to mark out and nobody came to build
situations.offer: give them a revision and they will show you the lodge

situations.doing: standing loaded with the rope cut and the load in the air
situations.onArrival: the load turns very slowly in no wind
situations.because: it was loaded for a shift that was never called
situations.offer: bring the load down and the whole quarter's scaffolding opens to you

situations.doing: hanging still in a tower over an empty site
situations.onArrival: the rope moves as though somebody has just let go
situations.because: the shift is rung at this hour and always has been
situations.offer: ring it and everything on the works comes, and does as it is told

temptations.cue: a wedge of the cut keystone
temptations.benefit: once, close something that was left open
temptations.standingDrawback: the works stop while you hold it, and notice why

temptations.cue: a sheet off the master drawing
temptations.benefit: know what this quarter was built to be
temptations.standingDrawback: the lodge wants the sheet back and will send for it

temptations.benefit: once, make a thing look as though it belongs here
temptations.standingDrawback: the mason knows their mark has been used

temptations.benefit: once, walk the works unchallenged
temptations.standingDrawback: you are on the shift, and the bell applies to you

temptations.cue: a stick of the works' chalk
temptations.benefit: once, mark out a way through a wall
temptations.standingDrawback: the works build what you marked, immediately

rolls.dangerLine: the city has everyone written down, and it has noticed that you are not

institution: a muniment room with a roll for every year and every ward
clerks' desks set so that nobody enters unseen
a roll called at the gate before anyone comes in
ritual: names entered at the gate and read back for confirmation
the rolls compared against each other each quarter
a name struck through with a single line, never scratched out
demand: a roll open at a blank line with the pen still wet
a desk with a chair drawn out and a form set square
a name read out at a gate, and a pause
wound: a roll with a season cut out of it and the ends sewn together
names struck through so hard the parchment is holed
a muniment room with the presses forced and the rolls sorted by somebody in a hurry
anchor: the roll with every name on it, including the struck-off
a clerk's hand that never varied in forty years

features: a roll open at a blank line
a pen still wet on a desk
a name struck through with one line
holes worn through struck-out names
a gate book left open
a press forced and re-sorted

decisions.cue: a roll lying open at a blank line with the pen still wet
decisions.cost: writing a name enrols it, permanently

resolve.success: you enter a name the city will accept and pass every gate and ward unchallenged
resolve.failure: you enter your own and the city has you: +1 Bane and it always knows where you are
resolve.orElse: leave the line blank; you are unaccounted for, and everything here reacts to that

decisions.cue: a name struck through with a single line, still legible underneath
decisions.cost: reading it is not the same as restoring it

resolve.success: you read the struck name and learn who the city decided had never come
resolve.failure: you restore it, and whatever it named comes back onto the rolls too
resolve.orElse: leave it struck; the ending has no name to give and must be improvised

decisions.cue: a roll with a season cut out of it and the ends sewn together
decisions.cost: the cut season is somewhere

resolve.success: you find the excised season at {priorCue} and learn what the city did that year
resolve.failure: you unpick the stitching and the roll will not lie flat again — the clerks notice
resolve.orElse: leave it sewn; that season stays out of every account here

decisions.cue: a gate book with a name read out and no answer written beside it
decisions.cost: answering to it enters you under that name

resolve.success: you answer to it and inherit the freedoms of whoever that was
resolve.failure: you answer and inherit their debts as well: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: stay silent; the gate does not open and the wall runs for miles

decisions.cue: a muniment press forced and the rolls sorted by somebody in a hurry
decisions.cost: the sorter was looking for one thing

resolve.success: you work out what they were looking for and get to it first
resolve.failure: you disturb the sort and the clerks begin again, with you in the room
resolve.orElse: leave the press; you never learn what was worth forcing it for

decisions.cue: a clerk's desk with a chair drawn out and a form set square
decisions.cost: sitting down is taking the post

resolve.success: you take the desk and the City treats you as its own officer for the delve
resolve.failure: you sit and cannot rise while there is anything left unentered
resolve.orElse: stay standing; you are a member of the public, and are handled as one

situations.doing: holding a pen over a blank line on a roll
situations.onArrival: it looks up and asks your name and parish
situations.because: the line cannot be left blank and nobody has come to fill it
situations.offer: give it a name and it will enter you as free of the city

situations.doing: reading names off a book to an empty road
situations.onArrival: it stops at a name with no answer beside it
situations.because: the roll is called before anyone comes in
situations.offer: answer to the name and the gate opens, and stays open behind you

situations.doing: comparing two rolls that will not agree
situations.onArrival: they push both toward you without looking up
situations.because: the rolls have disagreed since the season that was cut out
situations.offer: tell them which is right and they will show you the muniment room

situations.doing: copying a struck-out name onto a fresh sheet
situations.onArrival: they cover the sheet when you enter and then uncover it
situations.because: somebody is paying them to put a name back
situations.offer: tell them who you are and they will sell you the name

situations.doing: holding a roll open at a name struck through with one line
situations.onArrival: it holds a finger on the line and waits
situations.because: the strike was made and never explained
situations.offer: read the name aloud and it will tell you exactly what was done and why

situations.doing: lying open on a desk in an empty room
situations.onArrival: the parchment is warm and the ink is not dry
situations.because: somebody was writing when the room emptied
situations.offer: read the last entry and the city admits what it has been doing since

temptations.cue: a strip cut from the great roll
temptations.benefit: once, be somebody the city has on its books
temptations.standingDrawback: whoever that was is unaccounted for now, and comes looking

temptations.benefit: once, make a thing officially true
temptations.standingDrawback: what you wrote is now true for everyone, not just you

temptations.benefit: know who came in and who never came out
temptations.standingDrawback: your own entry is in it, and can be read

temptations.benefit: once, be from anywhere you say you are
temptations.standingDrawback: the ward you claimed expects you at its wardmote

temptations.cue: a name struck off the rolls
temptations.benefit: once, be nobody at all
temptations.standingDrawback: the city cannot help you either while you are nobody

wards.dangerLine: everything here belongs to a ward, and the wards are still checking which

institution: boundary marks set into the paving every hundred paces
a wardmote for each quarter, meeting on its own night
posts and chains across the streets between wards
ritual: the bounds of each ward beaten once a year
chains drawn across the ends of streets at curfew
a question asked at every boundary: which ward
demand: a chain drawn across a street with nothing either side
a boundary mark with the ward name worn off
a post standing where two wards meet, and a space around it
wound: boundary marks prised up and reset wrongly
a ward that no longer answers when its bounds are beaten
chains left drawn across streets that go nowhere
anchor: the chain of office, still warm
a plan of the wards with every bound marked
a boundary mark that has never been moved

features: a chain drawn across an empty street
a boundary mark with the name worn off
a post at the meeting of two wards
marks prised up and reset
a ward plan pinned to a door
a curfew chain hanging loose

decisions.cue: a chain drawn across a street with nothing on either side of it
decisions.cost: stepping over is trespass; unhooking it is worse

resolve.success: you ask leave of the ward properly and it drops the chain for you
resolve.failure: you step over and the ward has you as a trespasser: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: go round through another ward, costing a Turn

decisions.cue: a boundary mark with the ward name worn off it
decisions.cost: which ward this is decides what is allowed here

resolve.success: you identify the ward from the plan and can claim its protections
resolve.failure: you guess wrong and claim protections from a ward that wants nothing to do with you
resolve.orElse: move on unplaced; everything here treats you as being from nowhere

decisions.cue: boundary marks prised up and reset a street further in
decisions.cost: somebody moved a ward's edge deliberately

resolve.success: you find who gained by the move and can hold the Wardmote to it
resolve.failure: you reset them yourself and both wards come to see who did: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave them; the wrong ward has jurisdiction over the route ahead

decisions.cue: a post standing where two wards meet with a clear space around it
decisions.cost: standing at the post makes you nobody's, briefly

resolve.success: you stand at the post and neither ward can touch you while you negotiate
resolve.failure: you stand there too long and both wards come to claim you
resolve.orElse: keep to one side; you are that ward's business entirely

decisions.cue: a curfew chain hanging loose at the end of a street
decisions.cost: drawing it shuts the street; leaving it open lets things through

resolve.success: you draw the chain and whatever is coming up the street stops at it
resolve.failure: you draw it with something already inside: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it hanging; the street is open both ways all night

decisions.cue: a ward plan pinned to a door with one ward inked over
decisions.cost: the inked ward is not on any other plan

resolve.success: you find the erased ward and can enter it, which nothing else here can
resolve.failure: you ask about it aloud and the Wardmote takes an interest in you
resolve.orElse: leave the plan; the ending happens somewhere you will not have been

situations.doing: sitting in a street with the chain drawn behind them
situations.onArrival: they turn as one and ask which ward you are from
situations.because: nobody may be in a ward without belonging to one
situations.offer: name a ward and they will escort you through it, and vouch for you

situations.doing: beating the bounds of a ward that no longer answers
situations.onArrival: it strikes a mark and waits for a reply that does not come
situations.because: the bounds are beaten annually and this year nothing answered
situations.offer: answer for the ward and it will beat you a way through the next one

situations.doing: waiting at a chain with a load and no patience
situations.onArrival: they ask whether you know whose street this is
situations.because: the chain went up and nobody has come to drop it
situations.offer: find whose street it is and they will carry you and your load anywhere

situations.doing: standing either side of a boundary mark, not crossing
situations.onArrival: each asks you what the mark says
situations.because: the name wore off and neither will concede
situations.offer: read it for them and the losing ward opens its gates to you

situations.doing: hanging drawn across a street with nothing either side of it
situations.onArrival: it tightens very slightly as you approach
situations.because: the curfew was drawn and never lifted
situations.offer: have it dropped properly and every chain in the quarter drops with it

situations.doing: standing at a post where two wards meet, in neither
situations.onArrival: it asks whose you are, and means it as a real question
situations.because: it was between wards when the city stopped and belongs to neither
situations.offer: claim it for a ward and it will give you the freedom of that ward entirely

temptations.benefit: once, close a street to whatever is coming
temptations.standingDrawback: what it stops waits for you at the other end

temptations.benefit: once, decide which ward something is in
temptations.standingDrawback: the ward you took it from has no edge at all now

temptations.benefit: know every bound and jurisdiction here
temptations.standingDrawback: you know which ward wants you, too

temptations.benefit: once, be an officer of a ward you are not from
temptations.standingDrawback: that ward's wardmote expects your report

temptations.benefit: once, stand where nothing has jurisdiction
temptations.standingDrawback: nothing has jurisdiction to protect you either

liberties.dangerLine: the city's writ runs to the walls and stops, and things here are very clear about which side you are on

institution: a bar across the road where the city's writ begins
liberties outside the walls where the city cannot reach
a charter read out at the gate once a year
ritual: the freedom given to apprentices at the end of their term
a sheriff's writ refused at the bar, ceremonially
sanctuary claimed at a door and granted for forty days
demand: a bar standing across a road with nobody at it
a sanctuary door standing open with the knocker down
a freedom made out and never collected
wound: a bar broken and the road open both ways
sanctuary taken by force out of a doorway
freedoms revoked in a single sitting, all of them
anchor: the key of the postern that is not on any plan
a freedom made out in a name nobody claimed

features: a bar across a road with nobody at it
a sanctuary knocker hanging down
a freedom made out and uncollected
a charter unrolled on a table
a postern with no plan of it
a writ refused and left

decisions.cue: a freedom of the city made out and never collected
decisions.cost: claiming it makes you free of the city, with everything that carries

resolve.success: you claim it and the City treats you as its own — nothing here may lay hands on you
resolve.failure: you claim it and are bound by the city's obligations too: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it uncollected; you are a foreigner here, and the wards act accordingly

decisions.cue: a sanctuary door standing open with the knocker down
decisions.cost: taking sanctuary buys forty days and costs the road

resolve.success: you claim sanctuary correctly and nothing in the city can touch you in this place
resolve.failure: you claim it and cannot leave the ground while anything is still pursuing you
resolve.orElse: stay outside; whatever is hunting in this ward has an open run at you

decisions.cue: a bar standing across a road with nobody at it
decisions.cost: the bar marks where the writ starts

resolve.success: you work out which side you want to be on and stay there to your advantage
resolve.failure: you cross without thinking and the wrong power has jurisdiction over you
resolve.orElse: turn back; the whole liberty is closed to you and the ending is inside it

decisions.cue: a charter unrolled on a table with the seal intact
decisions.cost: the charter says what the city may and may not do

resolve.success: you find the clause the city has been breaking and can hold it to its own charter
resolve.failure: you break the seal and the charter is void, and so is every protection under it
resolve.orElse: leave it rolled; you have no leverage over anything official here

decisions.cue: a sheriff's writ refused at the bar and left lying
decisions.cost: the writ names somebody the city wanted

resolve.success: you read the name and learn who ran to the liberties and why
resolve.failure: you serve the writ yourself and the liberty treats you as the city's creature
resolve.orElse: leave it; whoever it names stays hidden and unhelpful

decisions.cue: a postern that is not marked on any plan of the walls
decisions.cost: it goes out, or something came in by it

resolve.success: you open it and have a way out of the city nothing here controls
resolve.failure: it opens outward and something that was waiting comes in: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave it shut; the only ways out are the gates, and the gates are watched

situations.doing: sitting inside a doorway with his feet on the threshold
situations.onArrival: he asks how many days you think he has left
situations.because: he claimed forty days and nobody ever came to count them
situations.offer: count for him and he will tell you every way out of the city

situations.doing: standing at a bar holding a writ nobody will take
situations.onArrival: it offers you the writ, patiently
situations.because: the writ was refused and cannot be withdrawn
situations.offer: take the writ and it will grant you the city's authority to serve it

situations.doing: arguing over which side of a bar a body is lying on
situations.onArrival: they stop and ask you to say
situations.because: jurisdiction depends on it and neither will yield
situations.offer: rule on it and the winning side owes you a hearing anywhere

situations.doing: waiting at a hall door with his term served
situations.onArrival: he asks whether they are giving out freedoms today
situations.because: his term ended and nobody came to make him free
situations.offer: make him free and he will take you anywhere in the city as one of its own

situations.doing: holding a charter and reading the same clause repeatedly
situations.onArrival: it looks up and asks whether that is what it says
situations.because: the charter was broken and it cannot find where
situations.offer: show it the clause and it will grant you anything within the charter

situations.doing: standing in a wall with no plan showing it
situations.onArrival: the lock is oiled and the hinges are clean
situations.because: it was kept off the plans on purpose and kept working
situations.offer: open it and the city loses its hold on you entirely

temptations.cue: an uncollected freedom of the city
temptations.benefit: the City treats you as its own
temptations.standingDrawback: the City's obligations apply to you as well

temptations.benefit: hold the city to its own written word
temptations.standingDrawback: it holds you to the parts that bind citizens

temptations.cue: a sanctuary knocker off its door
temptations.benefit: once, be untouchable where you stand
temptations.standingDrawback: you cannot move from that spot while it holds

temptations.cue: the key of the unmarked postern
temptations.benefit: once, leave or enter unrecorded
temptations.standingDrawback: something else knows the postern now

temptations.benefit: once, compel anything of the city
temptations.standingDrawback: the liberties will not have you afterwards
